source.title: Towards Error Centric Intelligence I, Beyond Observational Learning

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives a conceptual challenge to a strict, reality-wide reading of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, arguing that observed alignment may be conditional on the ERM+SGD pipeline. It reports no new empirical test.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses PRH and presents theoretical arguments about observational versus interventional adequacy. The cited FER result is from other work, not a result of this study; no empirical outcome is reported that qualifies as a row.
record.test_reason: A theoretical position paper with no experiments and no representation-similarity measurements. Its challenge to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) concerns interventional competence: observationally equivalent causal models differ under do(). That is a different construct from whether representations converge. Its claim that convergence is 'pipeline-conditional' (an ERM+SGD bias) is asserted, not argued with results. The only empirical support it offers is the fractured–entangled representation (FER) result from Kumar et al. 2025, which is other work. So it discusses the claim rather than testing any version. The reader's T5/tests classification is too strong: T5 needs results or a specific argument that a version is wrong, and none of the paper's arguments bears on whether alignment occurs.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue AGI progress is theory-limited, not data- or scale-limited. On PRH, they argue observational adequacy does not secure interventional competence. They treat PRH evidence as pipeline-conditional (ERM+SGD), not as an insight into reality. Their main contribution is the error-centric framework (LAP, gauge-invariant ICM, CAP), not a test of PRH.
record.recipe_differences: No empirical reproduction or representation-similarity method is used.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical argument (Proposition 1, after Pearl): observationally equivalent structural causal models (SCMs) yield different interventional laws. So no encoder trained only on observational data can support arbitrary interventional heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Converged observational representations do not guarantee interventional or counterfactual competence. This is a claim about downstream causal adequacy, not about representational alignment.

record.problems: No new empirical results test representation alignment. The challenge is theoretical and refers to findings from other work; it does not establish that alignment changes under interventions or that the scale trend fails.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows. The cited FER finding in Section 2.2 is from other work and is not recorded as a result of this study.

untested.parts: No measurement of alignment across scale, architectures, objectives or data. The argument targets a strict reading (encoder suffices for interventional queries), not the convergence trend itself.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests.
No feature or circuit universality tests.
No metric, neighbour-count or input-distribution sensitivity analysis.
Suggests the ERM+SGD pipeline rather than reality may explain convergence, but gives no result showing this. It also does not measure incompleteness or plateau.

record.verdict_notes: No rows and no verdicts. The pipeline-conditional reading relates to V7's 'other causes', but it is an unsupported suggestion resting on a cited FER result, not on this study's own results. Recommend reclassifying from tests/T5 to discusses/T6.

versions.untested_parts: No direct measurement of alignment across model scale, capability, architectures, objectives, or training data; no empirical test of the scale-performance relationship.
Cross-modal alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions.
Convergent learning across random seeds, shared features, or subspaces.
Mapping or stitching representations across models, relative representations, and alignment without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Sensitivity of measured convergence to similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.

No empirical test of whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, nor whether alignment is incomplete or plateaus. The paper's alternative explanation is that observed convergence may reflect the ERM+SGD pipeline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
